sections.label: CPF Bill changes
sections.summary: The Bill closes the SA for those aged 55 and above, expands HPS cover, and clarifies CPF Board administration.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Bill effects the following changes: first, the CPF Special Account (SA) will be closed for those aged 55 and above from early 2025 onwards; second, the Bill expands the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) to offer cover to CPF members with certain pre-existing conditions that are not so severe; and lastly, the Bill introduces amendments to clarify processes and streamline the administration of the CPF Board and CPF schemes.

sections.label: SA closure for over-55s
sections.summary: From the second half of January 2025, members aged 55 and above will have their SA closed, leaving three CPF accounts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: From the second half of January 2025 onwards, the SA of members aged 55 and above will be closed and they will have just three CPF accounts.

sections.label: ERS raised to four times BRS
sections.summary: With the ERS raised to four times the BRS from 1 January 2025, over 99% of members aged 55 and above could transfer all SA savings to their RA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: With the ERS raised to four times the Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) from 1 January 2025, more than 99% of CPF members aged 55 and above today would be able to transfer all their SA savings to their RA, if they wish to do so.

sections.label: HPS expansion for pre-existing conditions
sections.summary: From mid-2025, HPS will be expanded to cover certain pre-existing conditions that are not so severe, such as certain strokes and heart disorders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: While we cannot cover all pre-existing health conditions, we will expand HPS from mid-2025 to cover those with certain pre-existing conditions that are not so severe, such as certain types of strokes and heart disorders.

sections.label: CPF Board composition
sections.summary: After the amendments, the Board will comprise a Chairperson, six tripartite representatives and eight other persons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: After the amendments, the Board will comprise a Chairperson, six tripartite representatives and eight other persons.

sections.label: Plus and Prime flat restrictions
sections.summary: Plus and Prime flats will have a 10-year MOP, and HDB may recover a percentage of resale price or market valuation commensurate with additional subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Plus and Prime flats will also come with additional restrictions, such as the 10-year minimum occupancy period (MOP), to discourage quick flipping and support genuine home buyers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This set of amendments will allow HDB to recover a percentage of the resale price or market valuation of the flat, whichever is higher, that is commensurate with the extent of additional subsidies provided.

sections.label: Long-term CPF savings interest rate
sections.summary: This ensures only long-term CPF savings can enjoy a higher long-term interest rate, effective from the second half of January 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This is to ensure that only long-term CPF savings can enjoy a higher long-term interest rate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This will take effect from the second half of January 2025.

sections.label: ERS increase from 2025
sections.summary: From 2025 onwards, the ERS will be increased to four times of the BRS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: From 2025 onwards, the ERS will also be increased to four times of the BRS.

sections.label: CPF Amendment Bill effects
sections.summary: The CPF (Amendment) Bill gives effect to closing the SA for members aged 55 and above, expanding the HPS, and clarifying CPF Board processes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The CPF (Amendment) Bill will give effect to the closure of the SA for members aged 55 and above from the second half of January 2025 onwards, as well as the expansion of the HPS to cover more CPF members with pre-existing health conditions from mid-2025 onwards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: It will also clarify processes and streamlines the administration of CPF Board and CPF schemes.

sections.label: Exception to SA closure
sections.summary: New section 13AA(1) provides an exception where the SA of a member aged 55 may not be closed if prescribed circumstances apply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 13AA(1) provides for an exception where the SA of a member who has attained 55 years of age may not be closed if any prescribed circumstances apply.

sections.label: CPF Board additional terms
sections.summary: The amendments allow the CPF Board to impose additional terms, such as excluding pre-existing health conditions and imposing premium loading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amendments will allow the CPF Board to impose additional terms, such as the exclusion of pre-existing health conditions and impose premium loading.

sections.label: Proportion of rejected HPS applications
sections.summary: The Minister was asked what proportion of the previously rejected 1.2% to 1.8% of HPS applications are expected to benefit from these amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Minister previously shared that about 1.2% to 1.8% of HPS applications were not approved due to serious pre-existing medical conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What proportion of the previously rejected 1.2% to 1.8% of HPS applications are expected to benefit from these amendments?

sections.label: HDB subsidy repayment from sale
sections.summary: Clauses 28 and 29 require owners of HDB flats with additional subsidies to prioritise repaying those subsidies from sale proceeds.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clauses 28 and 29, taken together, require that owners of HDB flats that have enjoyed additional subsidies to prioritise the repayment of said subsidies from proceeds, following the sale of the flat.

sections.label: HDB pricing model liquidity effects
sections.summary: Higher sticker prices are de-emphasised due to subsidies, but nominal-price valuations and loans plus full cash subsidy repayment can cause a liquidity crunch for sellers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: More generally, this is one of the unintended consequences of the current HDB pricing model, where a higher sticker price is de-emphasised simply because subsidies mean that the de facto price faced by buyers would be lower.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But if valuations and, perhaps more importantly, mortgage loans are still based on the nominal price, and we insist on subsidies being fully repaid in cash, then we inadvertently impose a liquidity crunch on those who wish to sell, since we strip these sellers of a significant part of the cash amounts that they would otherwise need as downpayments on their next flat.

sections.label: WP position on loophole closure
sections.summary: The Workers' Party is not opposed in principle to closing this loophole, which tended to benefit a relatively select group.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For these reasons, the Workers' Party (WP) is not opposed, in principle, to the closure of this loophole, given how it tended to benefit this relatively select group.

sections.label: CPF withdrawal loophole closure
sections.summary: Allowing account holders to withdraw funds at will while promising higher returns threatens CPF's long-term investments, so this unsustainable loophole had to be closed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But when we promise higher returns but still allow account holders to withdraw their funds at will, we short-circuit this process, which threatens to unravel the otherwise sound long-term investments that CPF will have taken exposure in.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Hence, given its inherent unsustainability, this loophole had to be closed.

sections.label: WP suggestions on CPF rates
sections.summary: The WP previously suggested raising CPF rates for inflation, using daily or monthly rates, and considering one-off adjustments to OA deposit and lending rates.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Part of this, surely, is that, despite assurances by the Government that the CPF rate is adequate for retirement, those that were taking advantage of this SA loophole clearly thought otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That is why the WP had, in this House, previously suggested that CPF rates be raised to reflect high inflation, that it be computed with daily or monthly rates to better harvest returns or that it also considers one-off adjustments to the OA rate, not just to deposit but also lending rates, which tend to better reflect the global cost of capital, among others.

sections.label: Expanding CPF-approved investments
sections.summary: Beyond re-examining OA interest rate calculation, the universe of CPF-approved investments should be expanded, as low-cost index fund options remain scarce.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This goes beyond re-examining how we calculate the OA interest rate, as important as that may be.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We should also look to expanding the universe of CPF-approved investments.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: At the moment, there remains a dearth of low-cost index fund options, for a portfolio of either domestic or internationally-diversified companies.

sections.label: CPF returns and HPS
sections.summary: Boosting CPF returns addresses members seeking returns through shielding or housing, while HPS protects CPF members from losing their HDB flat on death, terminal illness or total permanent disability.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Further bolstering the returns available from CPF savings, through ways I have described, will strike at the heart of the problem that has led many to hunt for returns via either shielding or housing.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: HPS is a mortgage-reducing insurance that protects CPF members from losing their HDB flat in the event of death, terminal illness or total permanent disability.

sections.label: Expanded HPS coverage question
sections.summary: A Member asks to what extent the expanded HPS would cover the 1.3% of HPS applications rejected in the last three years due to serious pre-existing medical conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, I appreciate the intention to expand the HPS to admit more CPF members.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I note that in the Minister's written answer in August 2024 to Member Ms Yeo Wan Ling's Parliamentary Question on coverage for the HPS, the Minister had replied that, "In the last three years, about 1.3% of HPS applications were rejected due to serious pre-existing medical conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The top reasons for such rejection is due to the applicant having multiple pre-existing medical conditions or cancer." I also note from the Minister's speech earlier that the expanded HPS would cover those with less severe pre-existing conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, similar with Member Louis Ng's point, to what extent would the expanded HPS cover this cumulative 1.3% of HPS applications that were rejected in the past three years due to serious pre-existing medical conditions?

sections.label: Section 32A premium loading
sections.summary: Section 32A provides for the Board to impose premium loading on a CPF member whose assessed health risk exceeds the Board's threshold, if other health-related criteria are met.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, I note that section 32A provides for the Board to impose premium loading on a CPF member whose assessed health risk exceeds the threshold determined by the Board, so long as the Board is satisfied that the member meets all other health-related criteria determined by the Board.

sections.label: Concern over premium loading
sections.summary: A Member states concern about the introduction of premium loading for residents with higher health risks under the HPS insurance scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, Mr Speaker, Sir, I am concerned about the introduction of premium loading for residents with higher health risks under the HPS insurance scheme.

sections.label: CPF Board additional premiums
sections.summary: Section 32A of the Bill allows the CPF Board to impose additional premiums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Section 32A of the Bill allows CPF Board to impose additional premiums.

sections.label: HPS rejections and conditions
sections.summary: Coverage depends on severity, prognosis and control of the condition and overall health, yet many HPS applications were rejected due to common pre-existing conditions like cancer, stroke or kidney failure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Instead, it depends on the severity, prognosis and control of the condition, alongside the individual's overall health profile.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, many HPS applications in recent years have been rejected due to common pre-existing conditions like cancer, stroke or kidney failure.

sections.label: CPF members appeal options
sections.summary: Asks what recourse or appeal CPF members have if rejected from extended HPS coverage or facing higher premiums after conditions improve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What avenues for recourse or appeal will CPF members have if their conditions improve but they are still rejected from extended HPS coverage or face higher premiums?

sections.label: Automatic closure of CPF SAs
sections.summary: States that automatic closure of CPF SAs at age 55 and transfer of funds to OA or RA streamlines CPF management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The automatic closure of CPF SAs at age 55 and the transfer of funds to the OA or RA, are a significant step towards streamlining CPF management.

sections.label: Timing of CPF SA closure
sections.summary: Asks the Minister to clarify when automatic closure of CPF SAs takes effect after a member turns 55.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One, could the Minister clarify when exactly the automatic closure of CPF SAs will take effect after a member turns 55?

sections.label: Expanded HPS eligibility
sections.summary: States the Bill expands HPS eligibility to individuals with serious conditions, subject to premium adjustments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Four, the Bill introduces expanded eligibility for the HPS, allowing coverage for individuals with serious conditions, subject to premium adjustments.

sections.label: SME support for CPF changes
sections.summary: Asks what support SMEs will get to manage internal system changes for new CPF procedures that may increase compliance burdens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Five, what support will be provided to small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to manage change of internal systems to handle the new CPF procedures that may increase compliance burdens for businesses, especially those with limited administrative resources?

sections.label: Extending coverage to excluded individuals
sections.summary: States about 1.3% of applications are rejected annually due to severe health issues, and the amendment extends coverage to those with serious but well-managed conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Yet around 1.3% of applications are rejected annually due to more severe health issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: With this amendment, we will extend coverage to those previously excluded, specifically individuals with serious but well-managed health conditions.

sections.label: Flat sale repayment priority
sections.summary: Owners must return a percentage of resale price or valuation, whichever is higher, with repayment priority after property tax and before other loans and refunds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Under the sale of these flats, owners must return to HDB a percentage of the resale price or the flat’s valuation, whichever is higher.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The repayment will take priority after any outstanding property tax and before HDB or bank loans, resale levies and CPF housing refunds.

sections.label: Notifying affected CPF members
sections.summary: Affected CPF members will be notified by hard copy letters and email or SMS about amounts transferred to their RA and OA after SA closure.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: All affected CPF members will be notified via hard copy letters and email or SMS, where applicable, informing them of the amounts that have been transferred into their RA and OA after their SA has been closed.

sections.label: CPF interest on transferred SA
sections.summary: SA savings transferred to the RA up to the FRS earn RA interest for that month, as CPF interest is computed monthly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As CPF interest is computed monthly, the SA savings that are transferred to the RA up to the FRS will earn the RA interest for that month.

sections.label: High-income members unable to transfer
sections.summary: About 8,400 high-income members, under 1% of members aged 55 and above, cannot fully transfer SA savings to RA even as ERS was raised.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, I will not touch on that further.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I want to highlight a point that today, there are about 8,400 members who are relatively high-income earners, representing less than 1% of all members aged 55 and above, who will not be able to — So, it is just this 8,400 members, about less than 1% of all members aged 55 and above, who will not be able to fully transfer their SA savings to their RA, even as we raised the ERS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: By the way, we have raised the ERS to four times up from the current three times of BRS.

sections.label: HPS application approvals
sections.summary: The vast majority of HPS applications are approved, including for members with pre-existing health conditions assessed to be generally in good health.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The vast majority of HPS applications are approved, including for members with pre-existing health conditions, if they have been assessed to be generally in good health.

sections.label: Expanded HPS coverage estimate
sections.summary: Examples include certain strokes and heart disorders, and the expansion is estimated to offer HPS coverage to about 100 more members each year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Examples would include certain types of strokes and heart disorders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We estimate that this expansion will offer HPS coverage to approximately 100 more members each year.

sections.label: CPF Board outreach to members
sections.summary: The CPF Board will reach out to members who may be eligible for cover under the expanded HPS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The CPF Board will reach out to such members that may be eligible for cover under the expanded HPS.

sections.label: HPS premiums in market
sections.summary: Even with premium loading, HPS would provide coverage at one of the lowest premiums in the current market for all members.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Even with premium loading, HPS would provide coverage at one of the lowest premiums in the current market for all members.

sections.label: Annual HPS premium reviews
sections.summary: To keep HPS premiums affordable, the CPF Board conducts premium reviews annually.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Members of the House, to ensure that HPS premiums remain affordable, the CPF Board conducts premium reviews annually.

sections.label: Subsidy recovery rate for flats
sections.summary: The recovery rate applies to the flat's resale price or prevailing market value, whichever is higher at the point of sale.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As Mr Chia has rightly pointed out, the recovery rate will be applied to the flats' resale price or prevailing market value, whichever is the higher at the point of sale.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: HDB informs flat buyers of the subsidy recovery rate up front at the point of launch and the recovery rate remains fixed at the point of resale, regardless of whether the flat was eventually sold at a profit or loss compared to the original launch price.

sections.label: Amendments impact on SMEs
sections.summary: The amendments are not expected to impact SMEs and employers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The amendments are not expected to impact SMEs and employers.
